speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Prime Minister with regard to CPFB's clarification on the case of Ms Sua Li Li (a) why was it not possible for "public interest" to be protected through the continued use of the pseudonym "Ms Soo"; (b) what was the definition of "public interest" adopted in this case; (c) what was the process that led to the decision made for personal data disclosure without consent; (d) whether a correction order under POFMA was considered given the claim that the article "contained misleading statements"; and (e) whether the Government will consider for all future personal data disclosures without consent to be mandatorily accompanied by justification from the agency on why disclosure is warranted and reasonable, as similarly prescribed by the Personal Data Protection Commission for non-exempted organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It is the duty of Government agencies to do so in order to maintain the public's trust and to serve citizens effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If citizens are misled about the Government's processes or policies, they may make decisions that are detrimental to themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It is, therefore, fully in the public interest to dispel such doubts and clarify the facts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The clarification included Ms Sua's full name, her interactions with various agencies, and the support that she and her daughter were receiving from multiple public agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Such data was included in order to convey verifiable facts and provide the public with the full picture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is necessary to ensure the public is not misinformed and public’s trust in the Government is maintained.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It also allowed Ms Sua to challenge the Government's account of the case, if need be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The type of personal data that was disclosed was discussed at length by the various agencies before a final decision was made.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In addition, TOC had initially published a letter from the Associate Consultant at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital to the Social Service Office at Yishun.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This contained Ms Sua's full name, date of birth, age and gender.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Ms Sua's name was subsequently removed by TOC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: On the matter of how the Government makes such factual clarifications, the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA) is only one of several means available to us to set the record straight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Government's response depends on a sensitive reading of the situation, calibrated according to what is necessary and appropriate in the circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In Ms Sua's case, the agencies assessed that issuing a public clarification was the appropriate response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Regardless of the action taken, online publishers should not make use of pseudonyms in order to hide behind the veil of anonymity, so that they can publish unverified facts or misleading statements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is not in the best interest of sound public debate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Ms Anthea Ong also asked whether the Government will consider, for all future personal data disclosures without consent, to be mandatorily accompanied by justification on why disclosure is warranted and reasonable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Ms Anthea Ong claimed in her Parliamentary Question that this was required by the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) for private sector organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In any case, both public and private sector organisations have to be ready to state the reasons and considerations behind the personal data disclosure, when required to do so.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The Government's press release states that the law permits such disclosure, including the identity of the individual and the public interest.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also just share how is the public interest defined in this case?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Also, could the Senior Minister of State share which law this disclosure is permissible under?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: And would the Senior Minister of State consider making the Government's Instruction Manuals publicly accessible, as practised in other countries and recommended also by the Public Sector Data Review Committee?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The second half of Ms Anthea Ong's question, Mr Deputy Speaker, has already been addressed in a number of Parliamentary Questions that I have personally answered and we have brought a discussion to this House.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not think there is anything extra in her question nor in any answer that I can give to that, between the Government's Instruction Manuals and the fact that these laws do exist under the Public Sector (Governance) Act.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I am sorry, what was the first point that the Member wanted to ask?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Because the press release stated that the law —

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Oh, public interest, the Member asked me about public interest.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If the Member can persuade me that that is so, I would be very surprised.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And I do not think the Member can persuade many people that there is some benefit to be gained about perpetuating disinformation and falsehoods about medical care, welfare benefits, social services, processes.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I understand that one of the disclosures made about Ms Sua was that she was suicidal.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I am wondering why is that a piece of information that was necessary to be disclosed in this case.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Ms Anthea Ong may be asking about a particular fact.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I think the question is misdirected to me.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, would Ms Anthea Ong like to rephrase her question?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I am actually asking, and I do stand corrected if I am wrong, but I understand that one of the pieces of information that was publicly disclosed by the Government was that Ms Sua is suicidal or was suicidal.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On this matter, as several that I have highlighted, I think Ms Anthea Ong needs to establish what the facts are and what the timeline of those facts are.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The articulation of those issues, the explanation and the clarification that were provided by the Government agencies, after quite a significant period of consultation, established the facts, the timeline and the chronology quite robustly.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not think we should add to any confusion in this debate.
